nodes.description: Loss of renal 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 activity, encoded by HSD11B2, fails to convert active cortisol to inactive cortisone in mineralocorticoid target tissues, allowing cortisol to accumulate at the mineralocorticoid receptor.

evidence.reference_title: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess: comprehensive overview of molecular genetics.
evidence.snippet: It is caused by defects in the HSD11B2 gene, encoding the enzyme 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (11β-HSD2), which is primarily involved in the peripheral conversion of cortisol to cortisone.

evidence.reference_title: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess syndrome: an overview.
evidence.snippet: This enzyme is co-expressed with the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) in the kidney and converts cortisol (F) to its inactive metabolite cortisone (E).

nodes.description: Because the mineralocorticoid receptor binds cortisol and aldosterone with similar affinity, unmetabolized cortisol illicitly activates the receptor, reproducing a mineralocorticoid-excess state despite suppressed aldosterone.

evidence.reference_title: Classic and Nonclassic Apparent Mineralocorticoid Excess Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Subtypes of essential hypertension characterized by low renin levels allowed the identification of 2 different clinical entities: aldosterone-mediated mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) activation and cortisol-mediated MR activation.

nodes.description: Plasma renin activity is suppressed by chronic volume expansion and hypertension.

evidence.reference_title: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess: comprehensive overview of molecular genetics.
evidence.snippet: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess is an autosomal recessive form of monogenic disease characterized by juvenile resistant low-renin hypertension, marked hypokalemic alkalosis, low aldosterone levels, and high ratios of cortisol to cortisone metabolites.

evidence.reference_title: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess syndrome: an overview.
